Yes—the units cancel, and the operation belongs on the speed type. The pending revision adds `NonnegativeSpeed::clamped_inverse_lerp(lower, upper) -> SpeedResult<UnitInterval>`, with typed bounds and rejection of nonincreasing intervals. Profile selection, ordinary step distance, pose sampling and authored stride calibration now use that operation instead of extracting speed scalars at each call site.

These changes are currently local and under review; they have not been pushed to the PR head yet.

comments.body:
I traced this exact callee through the pinned Bevy/glam source. It is the external `FloatExt` implementation for `f32`, whose body computes `self + (rhs - self) * t`. `CycleDelta::checked_lerp` already accepts typed endpoints and `UnitInterval`; extraction happens immediately at that external arithmetic call, and the result is checked before becoming `CycleDelta` again. There is no intervening application API on this particular path.

The wider trace did expose application-level propagation gaps. M04 was already in the ledger, but its chain stopped too early. The trace now includes all four run-fraction producers, their stride and pose consumers, and height compensation. Height compensation was reconstructing the fraction by dividing flight heights, including a valid zero denominator. The pending revision carries typed fractions through those operations and derives the height compensation fraction directly from speed. This completes the connected trace for this repair; the broader audit ledger is still unfinished.

comments.body:
Yes. The pending revision implements the arithmetic on the existing types:

- `NonnegativeSpeed - NonnegativeSpeed` produces `SignedSpeed`.
- `SignedSpeed * UnitInterval` produces `SignedSpeed`.
- `NonnegativeSpeed + SignedSpeed` returns a checked nonnegative speed.
- `SignedSpeed / SignedSpeed` returns a checked, dimensionless `Ratio`, rejecting zero divisors and nonfinite results.

Interpolation and normalization now compose those typed operations. The general quotient reuses the existing `Ratio` owner; only bounded normalization converts it to `UnitInterval`, since arbitrary ratios may be negative or greater than one. Primitive field access remains inside the owning arithmetic implementations.

Agreed. The pending revision removes `smoothstep01`. This call becomes:

```rust
let progress = UnitInterval::from_fraction(half.fract())?.smoothstep()?;
```

`smoothstep` remains a method on `UnitInterval`, so its input stays typed. The explicit fallible conversion admits the native phase coordinate; the returned progress also remains typed through its comparisons, complement and conversion into blend weights.

Magic number. My Codex side chat says:

> It encodes the assumption that contact starts at `0.5`, leaving an interval of length `0.5`.
> 
> The intended normalization is:
> 
```rs
progress = (phase - contact) / (1 - contact)
```
> 
> The scale should be derived from those endpoints, ideally inside a typed interval-normalization operation. That keeps the contact phase as the single source of truth.

It encodes the assumption that contact starts at 0.5, leaving an interval of length 0.5.

The intended normalization is:

progress = (phase - contact) / (1 - contact)

The scale should be derived from those endpoints, ideally inside a typed interval-normalization operation. That keeps the contact phase as the single source of truth.
